label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores averaging only 0.81, PHQ-9 depression scores at 0.32, and GAD-7 anxiety scores near floor at 0.04, these individuals demonstrate consistently strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal feelings of loneliness or social isolation
Maintains moderate and controlled screen or internet usage (1–3 hours daily)
Demonstrates stable emotional and psychological functioning across multiple well-being indicators

label: High-Distress Heavy-Screen-Time Graduate Women
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on screens and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness scores (mean 1.72), PHQ-9 depression scores (mean 1.76), and GAD-7 anxiety scores (mean 2.18) are all in the higher range, indicating a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress across all three domains, with anxiety being the most pronounced.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Shows the highest distress on anxiety measures (GAD-7 mean 2.18)
Engages in heavy daily screen use (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounded psychological burden
tone: Emotionally burdened and anxious, reflecting a pattern of pervasive psychological distress

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With mean scores well below clinical thresholds on all three measures (UCLA-8 loneliness: 1.25, PHQ-9 depression: 0.82, GAD-7 anxiety: 0.85), these individuals demonstrate strong psychological well-being. They are predominantly male with graduate-level or higher education and report moderate daily screen or internet use of 1–3 hours.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports very low loneliness, well below the scale midpoint (mean 1.25 on UCLA-8)
Exhibits minimal depressive symptoms (mean 0.82 on PHQ-9, indicating negligible depression)
Displays very low anxiety levels (mean 0.85 on GAD-7, well under clinical concern thresholds)
Maintains moderate and controlled screen/internet use (1–3 hours daily)
Represents a sizable and stable subgroup (n=324 in training data)
tone: Calm, stable, and psychologically resilient — reflecting a well-functioning individual with minimal emotional distress
